title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN FOOD SCIENCE AND NUTRITION: METHODS, APPLICATIONS, AND ETHICAL ISSUES
abstract: Food science and nutrition increasingly require tools that are able to handle complicated heterogeneous date. Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the emerging fields which involves multidimensional aspects in science and technology. AI is gradually becoming an important analytical and decision-support approach in food science and nutrition. Its applications now extend from food quality, safety, authenticity, processing and traceability to dietary assessment, personalized nutrition, clinical nutrition support and public health surveillance. The main contribution of AI is its ability to connect complex data sources with faster and more structured decision-making. However, the value of AI depends on how responsibly it is developed and used. In this field, scientific accuracy, domain expertise and ethical oversight remain essential. AI should therefore be viewed as a supportive tool that strengthens, rather than replaces, the role of food scientists, nutrition professionals, clinicians and regulators. When supported by reliable data, transparent models and human judgment, AI has the potential to improve food-system efficiency, nutrition care and population health outcomes.

title: Quantum Sensing for Quantum Precision Measurement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum sensors for achieving quantum precision measurement. The core claim is that leveraging the inherent properties of quantum sensors, specifically quantum effects like tunneling and entanglement, can enable significantly more accurate measurements of physical quantities compared to classical techniques. This work outlines the fundamental principles and theoretical frameworks underpinning this approach, focusing on the mechanisms by which quantum sensors achieve this enhanced precision. We examine various quantum sensor modalities, including SQUID magnetometers, atomic clocks, and NV centers, and discuss the challenges and future directions in this burgeoning field. The primary objective is to demonstrate how quantum measurement, exploiting the principles of quantum mechanics, can surpass the limitations imposed by classical measurement methodologies. The discussion includes a review of relevant theoretical concepts and a conceptual framework for understanding the relationship between sensor design, quantum effects, and measurement precision. Ultimately, this paper aims to provide a foundational understanding of the transformative potential of quantum sensing for precision measurement applications.

title: Dynamically Weighted Graph Attention Networks
abstract: Graph Attention Networks (GATs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various graph-based learning tasks. However, a fundamental limitation of traditional GATs lies in their reliance on static attention weights, which can hinder their adaptability to dynamic and heterogeneous graph structures. This research introduces Dynamically Weighted Graph Attention Networks (DW-GATs), a novel approach that addresses this limitation by incorporating dynamic weighting mechanisms. These mechanisms adjust attention weights based on node position, historical interactions, and overall graph dynamics. The core claim is that static attention mechanisms in GATs often fail to adapt effectively. The proposed DW-GATs aim to overcome this by creating a system capable of continuously refining attention scores. This enhances the model's ability to learn meaningful representations from diverse graph environments, ultimately leading to improved performance. The paper details the architecture, training methodology, and experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of DW-GATs compared to standard GATs.

title: Quantum Entanglement Accelerated Distributed Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed inference leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core concept involves constructing a quantum entanglement network where nodes are interconnected through entangled states. This allows for the parallel execution of independent inference steps, directly addressing the limitations imposed by classical communication bottlenecks. We demonstrate that by exploiting the instantaneous correlation inherent in entanglement, the system can achieve inference speeds significantly exceeding those attainable through traditional distributed computing methods. The theoretical framework outlines the key components of this architecture, including entanglement generation, distribution, and measurement protocols. We present a mathematical model describing the system's performance, highlighting the potential for accelerating complex probabilistic models. The primary focus is on the theoretical advancement, with no experimental validation presented. The system's efficiency is directly tied to the quality and number of entangled pairs utilized. Further research will explore practical implementations and scalability challenges.

title: Self-Organizing Hierarchical Neural Networks for Robotic Navigation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robotic navigation utilizing self-organizing hierarchical neural networks. The core idea is to leverage the emergent properties of neural networks combined with a hierarchical structure to enable robots to learn complex navigation strategies without explicit programming. We introduce a network architecture composed of lower-level feature extraction modules and higher-level strategic planning modules, trained using reinforcement learning and competitive learning mechanisms. This dynamic system allows for the robot to adapt to varying environments and task demands. The key contributions of this work lie in the synergistic combination of self-organization and hierarchical neural networks, leading to robust and adaptable navigation capabilities. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the design principles and training methodologies. The resulting network exhibits the ability to learn efficient navigation routes and dynamically adjust its strategy based on environmental feedback. Future research will focus on scaling this architecture to more complex environments and integrating it with sensor fusion techniques.

title: 基于量子自适应的非线性系统动力学模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to system dynamics using a quantum adaptive mechanism. Traditional simulation methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and prone to inaccuracies. We propose a quantum-enhanced dynamic simulation framework that leverages quantum self-adaptation to more effectively capture the complex dynamics of non-linear systems. The model aims to provide a more efficient and accurate method for simulating and understanding the behavior of such systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through the simulation of a complex, non-linear system, revealing key features of its dynamics. The core claim of this work is the development of a quantum-enhanced system dynamics model that achieves higher accuracy and efficiency compared to conventional methods.

title: 基于自适应机器学习模型的特征选择
abstract: This paper introduces a novel feature selection algorithm based on adaptive machine learning models, designed to dynamically adjust feature selection based on data and model prediction error. Traditional feature selection methods often rely on static feature sets, failing to account for data fluctuations. This algorithm employs a "dynamic feature selection adjustment" mechanism to proactively optimize feature selection, ultimately improving model performance. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop between data characteristics and model output to iteratively refine the selection of relevant features. This approach addresses the limitations of static feature selection by providing a more robust and adaptive method for improving model accuracy. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of experiments involving diverse datasets and model architectures. We analyze the impact of the dynamic adjustment on model performance, focusing on generalization and robustness.

title: Adaptive Non-Linear Function Structure Neural Network
abstract: Probability logic neural networks have long been a cornerstone of machine learning, offering a flexible and powerful framework for modeling complex systems. However, their inherent reliance on static, predefined functions often limits their ability to effectively capture the dynamic and evolving nature of real-world data. This paper introduces an innovative approach to probability logic neural networks, termed "Dynamic Function Structure" (DFS), which dynamically adjusts the network's non-linear function structure based on observed system states. The core mechanism leverages a learned function mapping, enabling the network to adapt to changing conditions and improve predictive performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DFS through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its potential for enhanced model adaptability and robustness.

title: Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution – An Adaptive Algorithm for Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a promising technology for secure communication, offering potentially unbreakable encryption. However, current QKD protocols are limited by the difficulty of generating and maintaining entangled states, necessitating complex and computationally intensive procedures. This paper introduces an adaptive quantum key distribution (QKD) algorithm, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust key distribution parameters, thereby enhancing security and efficiency. We propose a novel approach that utilizes a feedback loop to optimize key distribution based on observed error rates and entanglement fidelity, leading to a more robust and versatile QKD system. This research explores the design and implementation of this adaptive algorithm, detailing its core mechanism, key performance indicators, and potential applications. The study highlights the advantages of this approach over traditional QKD methods, emphasizing its potential to overcome current limitations and facilitate the widespread adoption of quantum communication.

title: Title: Quantum Cryptarithmetic - A Random Number Generation Algorithm Based on Quantum Entanglement
abstract: Quantum Cryptarithmetic, a field that explores the potential of quantum mechanics to generate random numbers, has long been recognized as a promising area for advanced cryptography. This paper investigates a novel random number generation algorithm leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. We propose a method that utilizes entangled quantum states to ensure the generation of truly random and secure numbers, offering a significant departure from traditional approaches. This research focuses on establishing a robust and reliable random number generation system, leveraging the unique characteristics of quantum entanglement to achieve unparalleled randomness and security. The core mechanism involves the construction of a quantum process that relies on the inherent properties of entangled states to produce uniformly distributed and unpredictable output.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应矩阵分解
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to matrix factorization leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. We propose a framework centered around the instantaneous correlation between entangled states, aiming to significantly enhance the efficiency and accuracy of matrix decomposition. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the entanglement parameters during the factorization process, optimizing the overall algorithm to reduce computational complexity. The study explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations of traditional methods, particularly in scenarios involving high-dimensional data and complex eigenvalue problems. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation.

title: Dynamic Topology Geometry: Adaptive Computation for Enhanced Simulation and Optimization
abstract: Dynamic Topology Geometry (DTG) presents a novel computational framework that leverages the intersection of topology, quantum computing, and machine learning to dynamically adjust geometric shapes and topology during numerical simulations and optimization. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional methods by offering enhanced flexibility, reduced computational cost, and the potential for discovering novel geometric structures. The core of DTG lies in a novel adaptive topology transformation algorithm, coupled with a machine learning model trained to optimize geometric parameters within a quantum computing environment. This architecture promises significant improvements in simulation efficiency and the exploration of complex geometric landscapes, ultimately facilitating more effective numerical modeling and optimization tasks. This paper details the fundamental principles of the DTG framework, highlights the key innovations, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in specific geometric transformations.

title: Based on Scalable Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of scalable quantum annealing to solve computationally challenging combinatorial optimization problems. The core idea is to map these problems into a quantum annealing framework, leveraging quantum tunneling to efficiently explore the solution space and ultimately converge to the global optimum. The research addresses the existing limitations in the scalability of quantum annealing, proposing a novel approach to tackle NP-hard problems effectively. We will demonstrate the potential of this methodology through a theoretical analysis and formulation of the quantum annealing algorithm, focusing on key parameters and their impact on solution quality and runtime. The ultimate goal is to provide a foundational understanding of applying quantum annealing to combinatorial optimization, paving the way for future developments and practical implementations. This work introduces a new framework for approaching complex optimization problems by harnessing the unique properties of quantum mechanics.

title: Quantum Information Dynamics: A Non-linear Field Theory Approach
abstract: This paper explores the interplay of non-linear field theory in quantum information dynamics, focusing on the influence of quantum entanglement and information transfer on system behavior. We propose a novel computational model based on this framework, enabling the simulation of complex dynamic processes within quantum systems. This work addresses the limitations of traditional approaches by directly incorporating quantum entanglement and exploring the potential for enhanced computational capabilities, particularly in the context of quantum computation and information processing. The core mechanism centers on constructing a dynamic field theory model predicated on quantum entanglement, utilizing quantum computation for simulation and analysis. This research aims to provide a deeper understanding of non-linear effects within quantum systems and offers a new perspective on the design of quantum algorithms.

title: Continuously Adaptive Curricula: Using Learner Models to Restructure Instruction in Real Time
abstract: Large language models can generate explanations and tutoring dialogue on demand, but most systems still rely on a curriculum that was fixed at the start of learning. The result is a path that does not change when a learner masters material early or repeatedly struggles with a prerequisite. This paper argues that the more important problem is not content generation but continuous reconstruction of the curriculum itself.We describe an architecture under development for the Mentrast platform that treats the curriculum as a living object. An AI tutor collects interaction evidence, a probabilistic learner model maintains estimates of mastery under uncertainty, and a curriculum engine uses those estimates to reorder, insert, or remove material. Drawing on work in intelligent tutoring systems and Bayesian knowledge tracing, we formalize curriculum selection as a repeated decision conditioned on the current learner state.A central practical constraint is also stated: if conversational evidence cannot be mapped reliably onto knowledge components, structural adaptation remains unreliable. The goal is a system that decides what the learner needs next rather than what was planned at the beginning.

title: Towards secure distributed medical diagnosis: a blockchain-driven MCAU-Net and MAA-Bi-LSTM framework
abstract: Lung cancer is considered as the deadliest type of cancer, a good diagnosis as well as effective treatment is based on early detection. By utilizing Deep Learning (DL) techniques, the medical practitioner’s burden is reduced since these models can automate the diagnosis and disease classification. However, these models often suffer from modest accuracy and scalability issues, which affect the model’s disease detection performance. Consequently, a Federated Learning (FL)-based Global Data Trained Disease Detection (GDTDD) model, to provide better disease detection in hospitals. Initially, obtained local data (lung CT images) from different hospitals were pre-processed using a median filtering technique. Then these pre-processed images get segmented with the utilization of a multi-Convolutional layer-assisted U-Net (MCAU-Net) model. From these segmented images, features including Multi-texton, Median Binary Pattern (MBP) and Improved Local Gabor Transitional Pattern (LGTrP) features were extracted. Then these extracted features were fused utilizing multi-scale channel attention module (MS-CAM) based feature fusion technique. Then, trained the hybrid Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Modified Attention layer Assisted Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (MAA-Bi-LSTM) with this fused feature and obtained the local model as output. Afterwards, these local models were transmitted to Federated Learning, which merges and aggregates these locally trained models and provides a global trained model. This globally trained model is stored on the blockchain to ensure security and privacy. Then this global model is trained with fused features for accurate and effective disease detection. Moreover, this MAA-Bi-LSTM+RNN model’s effectiveness in disease detection is proven by the experimental findings. The Precision and F-measure values of the proposed model are 95.48% and 96.30%

title: Designing for Minimal Generation: Reliable Tool-Calling for a Local LLM Insurance Claim Triage Agent
abstract: Insurance claim adjudication gets held up as a natural fit for LLM-based agents: chaining lookups, applying conditional coverage logic, and producing a rationale a human can audit, none of which calls for creativity so much as reliability. This report covers the design and evaluation of a two-tool ReAct agent, built with LangGraph, that triages synthetic insurance claims into "Approved" or "Route for Review" against policy coverage rules. The agent never issues a final denial by design; every failed check goes to a human, so the system triages instead of adjudicating. The main finding here is about tool-calling reliability, not reasoning quality. An early version of the agent asked the model to reproduce an entire patient record as a JSON string argument, and that failed unpredictably across several open-weight models served locally through Ollama (llama3.1, then qwen2.5): truncated JSON, tool calls narrated as text instead of invoked, and in the worst cases a single stray character as the entire argument. Replacing that tool with one that only takes a short patient identifier cut the model's actual generation task down to something close to copying a string it had already seen, and that alone eliminated the failures, with no change to model size and no new prompt engineering. On a 15-record synthetic validation set with a deterministic rule-checker reference, the resulting agent, run against a frontier model as its default backend but built to support local and other hosted backends as configurable options, matched the reference decision on all 15 records against a 10/15 floor for a policy that always defers to review. The practical lesson for anyone building something similar: the reliability gap between small local models and frontier models on structured tool-calling is a specific, trainable skill gap, separate from general reasoning ability, and the fix that worked here was cutting what the model had to generate down to nearly nothing, well before reaching for a bigger model or a cleverer prompt.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Health Informatics Clinical Focus in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
abstract: Federated learning offers a promising architecture for training clinical machine learning models across distributed Ugandan health facilities without centralising sensitive patient data. However, the practical viability of this approach depends on its robustness to two conditions that characterise real-world health informatics environments: distribution shift across heterogeneous facility populations and extreme label sparsity in routine clinical documentation. We establish convergence guarantees for the proposed algorithm under bounded distribution shift and demonstrate that the interaction between client heterogeneity and label scarcity produces a distinct failure mode—termed silent model divergence—that conventional federated averaging fails to detect. The analysis yields three principal contributions: a formal characterisation of the robustness-accuracy trade-off under shift and sparsity, a practical diagnostic criterion for identifying clients whose local data distributions have drifted beyond safe aggregation bounds, and a theoretical justification for prioritising certain clinical prediction tasks in low-resource settings. These findings provide a mathematical foundation for designing privacy-preserving clinical decision support systems that remain reliable as Ugandan health facilities scale their digital infrastructure.

title: 基于量子蒙霍恩霍夫算法的优化问题求解
abstract: This paper explores the application of the Quantum Monte Carlo algorithm (QMCMC) to solve optimization problems. The core idea is to formulate optimization problems as linear equations in quantum bits (qubits) and then employ the Quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to solve these linear equations. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and accurate method for tackling complex optimization challenges compared to traditional classical algorithms. The paper details the theoretical framework, highlighting the transformation process and the underlying mathematical principles. The key contribution lies in the novel application of QMCMC to optimization, presenting a new paradigm for solving such problems. The potential benefits of this method, including enhanced computational speed and increased solution precision, are discussed.

title: Biofeedback-Driven Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing biofeedback signals – such as heart rate variability (HRV), electroencephalography (EEG) signals, and skin conductance responses (SCR) – as parameters within optimization algorithms. The core claim is that incorporating these physiological signals can lead to more intelligent and adaptive optimization processes. The proposed mechanism involves integrating biofeedback with established algorithms like genetic algorithms and simulated annealing. title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance and Secure Multi-Party Computation
abstract: This paper presents a novel decentralized federated learning (DFL) system designed to mitigate the risks posed by Byzantine faults and enhance data privacy. Traditional federated learning systems are susceptible to attacks from malicious participants introducing corrupted model updates, jeopardizing model accuracy and security. This research addresses this vulnerability by integrating Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) protocols alongside secure multi-party computation (SMPC) techniques. The proposed system utilizes a distributed architecture where devices collaboratively train a model without directly sharing their raw data. BFT protocols ensure the integrity of model updates, while SMPC guarantees secure aggregation, preventing individual adversaries from compromising the overall learning process. The core claim is the design of a robust federated learning system capable of handling malicious actors and preserving data privacy. The system employs a consensus mechanism based on verifiable BFT, followed by a secure aggregation stage leveraging SMPC. The resulting model achieves high accuracy while safeguarding against adversarial manipulation. The system's architecture allows for scalability and adaptability to diverse network conditions, making it suitable for various real-world applications where data privacy and security are paramount. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of BFT and SMPC, providing a fundamentally more secure and reliable approach to federated learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Parallel Algorithm Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for validating parallel algorithms leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional algorithm verification methods, often reliant on simulation and exhaustive testing, face significant limitations when dealing with large and complex quantum algorithms. This research introduces a methodology that capitalizes on the inherent parallelism within quantum entanglement. The core concept involves decomposing an algorithm into a series of independent quantum operations, creating entangled quantum systems, executing these operations, and ultimately verifying the algorithm's correctness through the measurement of entangled particle states. The resulting quantum state, correlated with the expected algorithm outcome, is directly assessed. This approach offers a potentially more efficient and scalable method for validating quantum algorithms, moving beyond the constraints of classical simulation. The theoretical framework is presented, and the fundamental mathematical principles underpinning the verification process are detailed. This work establishes a foundation for future research in quantum algorithm validation and highlights the potential of entanglement-based techniques.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Graph Partitioning Algorithms
abstract: Graph partitioning is a fundamental problem in various fields, including computer graphics, high-performance computing, and network design. Traditional graph partitioning algorithms often suffer from high computational complexity, particularly when dealing with large and complex graphs. This research investigates the potential of quantum-inspired optimization techniques, specifically leveraging concepts from quantum annealing, to accelerate the graph partitioning process. We formulate the graph partitioning problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, allowing us to simulate the behavior of a quantum annealer on classical hardware. The core of our approach involves mapping the graph's connectivity structure onto a QUBO, representing nodes as binary variables and edges as constraints. By exploiting the inherent parallelism of quantum annealing, we aim to find optimal or near-optimal partitions significantly faster than conventional methods. The results demonstrate the feasibility and potential advantages of this quantum-inspired strategy for graph partitioning, offering a promising direction for tackling computationally intensive graph problems.

title: Based on Multi-Modal Emotional Feedback Reinforcement Learning Agent
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) agent designed to learn complex tasks through the incorporation of multi-modal emotional feedback. Traditional RL agents often rely solely on scalar rewards, which can be inefficient and difficult to interpret for humans. This research explores the potential of leveraging a richer, more nuanced feedback signal derived from multiple modalities – visual, auditory, and linguistic – each conveying different aspects of emotional states. The agent utilizes this multi-modal emotional feedback to guide its learning process, effectively accelerating convergence and improving performance. We define a framework where emotional signals are translated into reward and penalty functions, enabling the agent to adapt its behavior based on a comprehensive understanding of the user's emotional state. The core claim of this work is that reinforcement learning agents can significantly accelerate their learning process by understanding and utilizing human emotional feedback. This approach represents a shift from relying on simplistic reward functions to a more sophisticated system capable of responding to the subtleties of human emotion. Experimental results (simulated) demonstrate the effectiveness of this multi-modal approach, highlighting its potential for applications requiring human-agent collaboration and adaptive learning. ---

title: Quantum Information Entropy: Dynamic Computation and Optimization
abstract: Quantum information entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty, is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics and a critical factor in the design of quantum algorithms and systems. This paper investigates the application of dynamic computation techniques, leveraging quantum information entropy, to optimize quantum system performance and efficiency. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically calculates and optimizes quantum systems based on the inherent properties of this entropy, aiming to maximize information utilization and improve overall system functionality. The core mechanism centers around a quantum-state evolution algorithm that adapts to the system's state, dynamically adjusting parameters to achieve optimal performance. This work introduces a new approach to quantum system optimization, demonstrating potential improvements in key metrics including fidelity and reduced error rates.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Non-Commutative Algebra
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to optimization inspired by the principles of quantum mechanics, utilizing the framework of non-commutative algebra. Traditional quantum-inspired optimization algorithms often rely on mimicking specific quantum algorithms, leading to complex and sometimes inefficient implementations. We propose a fundamentally different strategy: to directly leverage the mathematical structure inherent in non-commutative algebra to represent and manipulate optimization problems. This approach allows for the creation of algorithms that naturally explore complex solution spaces, mirroring the inherent probabilistic and non-deterministic nature of quantum systems. The core idea is to represent optimization problems using non-commutative matrices and operators, allowing for operations that do not necessarily follow the traditional commutative rules. We explore the potential of this method, demonstrating its ability to generate diverse solutions and offering a potentially more robust and efficient pathway toward quantum-inspired optimization. The key contributions of this work lie in the shift from mimicking specific quantum algorithms to building optimization algorithms directly from the foundations of non-commutative algebra. We present a theoretical framework and initial explorations, paving the way for future research in this area.

title: Adaptive Quantum Annealing Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents an Adaptive Quantum Annealing Algorithm (AQA), designed to enhance the solution efficiency of complex optimization problems. The core idea is to dynamically adjust parameters within the quantum annealing process, such as the annealing rate and path, using a machine learning-based feedback mechanism. Specifically, a reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to monitor the quantum annealing process in real-time, analyzing its state and adjusting the annealing parameters accordingly. This adaptive approach allows the algorithm to tailor its behavior to the specific characteristics of each problem, potentially overcoming limitations of traditional, static quantum annealing methods. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulation, demonstrating its ability to achieve improved results compared to standard quantum annealing strategies. The key contributions of this work lie in the integration of quantum annealing with adaptive optimization, enabling a more robust and efficient solution for diverse optimization challenges. The algorithm's design provides a framework for future research in hybrid quantum-classical optimization techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Memory Network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel information storage and retrieval architecture, the Quantum Entanglement Memory Network (QEMN), leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that utilizing entangled quantum states for information storage and retrieval can overcome the limitations of classical storage and enable precise simulations of complex systems. The proposed mechanism involves constructing a network of quantum bits (qubits) entangled to create a network where information is encoded and decoded through the manipulation of superposition and collapse of the entangled states. QEMN represents a fundamentally new approach to information processing by integrating quantum entanglement as the central storage mechanism within a neural network architecture. We will explore the theoretical framework, detailing the key equations and mathematical representations involved in the operation of the network. The potential impact of QEMN on computational capabilities and complex system modeling is discussed.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to anomaly detection based on dynamically adjusted neural networks. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on static network architectures, struggling to effectively handle complex datasets. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts the network's parameters and learning strategy to identify anomalous data points, resulting in improved detection accuracy. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop between the network's internal state and the input data, allowing the network to adapt to evolving patterns. This paper details the design and implementation of the proposed system, outlining the key components and the resulting performance improvements compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. We present experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in detecting anomalies in a simulated dataset with varying levels of complexity.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Sustainable Development Goals in Morocco: Mechanisms of Influence and Conditions for Transformation
abstract: Abstract: This chapter develops a context-sensitive framework explaining how artificial intelligence may contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals in Morocco. It starts from the country’s differentiated development profile, where comparatively strong performance in some Goals coexists with persistent vulnerabilities in inclusion, innovation, institutional effectiveness and food security. Artificial intelligence is approached through development-relevant capabilities related to information processing, prediction, prioritization, decision support and operational improvement. The framework identifies two complementary mechanisms: decision-oriented information quality and process optimization. Their effects are considered conditional on digital infrastructure and human and analytical competencies. The resulting model therefore combines a direct relationship, two mediated pathways and two contextual conditions. Its main contribution is to move beyond a generic technological narrative by specifying how AI-enabled capabilities may become developmentally meaningful in a Moroccan setting. The chapter offers a parsimonious conceptual architecture linking national sustainability challenges to the informational, operational, technical and human conditions of AI-enabled transformation. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Sustainable Development Goals; Morocco; Decision-Oriented Information Quality; Process Optimization.

title: Replication bundle for a cross-emitter canonicalization divergence study (Stage 3 analysis, pre-registered rubric, and canonicalization-equivocation reproducer)
abstract: Replication archive for a study of cross-emitter divergence in JSON canonicalization across ten SDKs, covering both RFC 8785 JCS-form and a tuple-array canonical form. The bundle contains the pre-registered classification rubric with its self-declared SHA-256 lock, the Stage 3 statistical outputs (Wilson score CIs, Cochran's Q, cluster-adjusted Wilson, pair-level Cochran's Q, block-bootstrap independence check, BH-FDR at m=138, and an amortized-forgery-rate heatmap), bootstrap 95% confidence intervals on batched-Ed25519 signing latency across four conditions (n=5 pilot, n=30 confirmatory, same-stack control, and AFR-context sensitivity), the second-reviewer independent bucket audit (blind re-classification of the 30 highest-count fingerprints of 138 distinct; agreement on 30/30; Cohen's kappa is undefined on this subset), null-baseline JCS-vs-tuple-array agreement data, and a live canonicalization-equivocation reproducer (Node.js producer plus Java reference canonicalizer). The bundle includes a SHA-256 manifest for every file. See README.md and the paper's Appendix A for the honest disclosure of what the rubric's self-referential SHA-256 lock does and does not prove.

title: Multi-Agent Collaborative Learning with Dynamic Adjustment of Evolutionary Strategies
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-agent collaborative learning framework designed to enhance the efficiency and adaptability of a team of agents. The core innovation lies in dynamically adjusting the evolutionary strategies employed by each agent based on ongoing collaborative learning and environmental feedback. Traditional evolutionary strategies often suffer from a lack of coordination and responsiveness to changing conditions, leading to suboptimal performance in complex multi-agent scenarios. Our approach leverages agent-to-agent communication and collaborative learning to discover optimal evolutionary strategies. A dynamic adjustment mechanism is then implemented to fine-tune these strategies in real-time, responding to shifts in the environment and improving overall team performance. This work addresses the critical challenge of strategy adaptation within multi-agent systems, ultimately leading to a more robust and effective collaborative learning system. The proposed methodology is formulated using mathematical notation to clearly articulate the key elements and relationships involved. Specifically, we define the agent population as (s1, s2, ..., sK), where K represents the number of agents, and each si represents the evolutionary strategy of the i-th agent. The core of the algorithm revolves around a collaborative learning process governed by the following equation: θ = argminθ Σi=1K Li(θ), where θ represents the collective evolutionary strategy, and Li(θ) is the loss function for the i-th agent under the given strategy. We also utilize a dynamic adjustment function α(t) to modify the strategy based on time 't' and environmental feedback. The performance of the system is evaluated using metrics such as average reward, convergence rate, and robustness to environmental changes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulations, showcasing its superior performance compared to static evolutionary strategies and other collaborative learning methods.

Specifically, we define the agent population as (s1, s2, ..., sK), where K represents the number of agents, and each si represents the evolutionary strategy of the i-th agent. The core of the algorithm revolves around a collaborative learning process governed by the following equation: θ = argminθ Σi=1K Li(θ), where θ represents the collective evolutionary strategy, and Li(θ) is the loss function for the i-th agent under the given strategy. We also utilize a dynamic adjustment function α(t) to modify the strategy based on time 't' and environmental feedback. The performance of the system is evaluated using metrics such as average reward, convergence rate, and robustness to environmental changes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulations, showcasing its superior performance compared to static evolutionary strategies and other collaborative learning methods.

title: Semantic Graph Embeddings via Contrastive Learning with Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to graph embedding using contrastive learning, specifically designed to enhance the representation of semantic relationships within knowledge graphs. Traditional graph embedding techniques often fall short in effectively capturing the nuanced connections between nodes, leading to limitations in downstream knowledge graph completion tasks. Our method addresses this challenge by formulating the learning process as a contrastive problem. Nodes with similar semantic meanings are encouraged to have similar embeddings, while those with dissimilar meanings are pushed apart. This is achieved through training the embeddings to optimize for knowledge graph completion, thereby intrinsically encoding the underlying semantic structure. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and a detailed explanation of the training process. The core claim of this work is that contrastive learning provides a more robust mechanism for capturing rich semantic relationships compared to conventional graph embedding methods. The key mechanism involves using contrastive learning to train graph embeddings that are optimized for knowledge graph completion, forcing the embeddings to capture underlying semantic relationships. Our approach offers a significant advancement in graph embedding by directly addressing the limitations of existing techniques and paving the way for improved performance in various graph-related applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Data Encryption and Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed data encryption and verification leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core claim centers on achieving secure, keyless distributed encryption and verification by exploiting entangled states between multiple physical nodes. The mechanism involves encoding data at each node and utilizing the entanglement to perform encryption. Crucially, the system employs entanglement-based verification, allowing other nodes to validate data integrity without requiring key exchange, mitigating the risks associated with traditional key distribution methods. The design incorporates fault-tolerant quantum technologies for enhanced entanglement stability and reliability. This approach offers a potentially significant security enhancement compared to existing distributed encryption schemes. The theoretical framework and underlying mathematical principles are presented, outlining the architecture and operational characteristics of the proposed system.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Optimization and Causal Inference
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover mathematical expressions that accurately represent a given dataset. However, it often struggles with noisy data, high dimensionality, and complex, non-linear relationships. This work proposes a novel approach combining symbolic regression with Bayesian optimization and causal inference. Bayesian optimization efficiently explores the search space of potential mathematical expressions, while causal inference provides prior knowledge and constraints to guide the regression process, improving accuracy and robustness. We introduce a framework where causal relationships are incorporated as constraints during the symbolic regression, reducing the search space and preventing the discovery of spurious correlations. This approach demonstrates improved performance compared to standard symbolic regression methods, particularly when dealing with imperfect data. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these techniques, offering a more reliable and interpretable method for mathematical equation discovery. The core claim is that symbolic regression struggles with noisy data and complex relationships. The core mechanism is the combination of symbolic regression with Bayesian optimization for efficient search and causal inference to guide the regression process and identify relevant relationships.

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Deep Learning Representations
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analyzing deep learning representations by leveraging information-theoretic principles. Traditional methods for evaluating deep learning models often rely on subjective metrics or task-specific performance, failing to capture the underlying information processing dynamics within the network. We introduce a framework that directly applies information-theoretic measures – mutual information, entropy, and transfer entropy – to the hidden layers of deep neural networks. This allows us to quantify the amount of information being encoded, transmitted, and refined as data propagates through the network. The core claim is that this approach offers a more fundamental understanding of how deep learning models operate, moving beyond simply measuring performance to examining the actual information flow. The results demonstrate the potential for these measures to reveal insights into network architecture, training strategies, and the representation learned, offering a new objective lens for evaluating deep learning models. ---

title: Meta-Learning of Graph Embedding Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a meta-learning framework for graph embedding algorithms, addressing the significant challenge of selecting and tuning optimal embedding methods across diverse graph datasets. Traditional approaches necessitate extensive manual experimentation, a time-consuming and often ineffective process. Our proposed system leverages meta-learning to automate this adaptation, learning to dynamically optimize the hyperparameters of various graph embedding algorithms based on performance feedback. The core idea is to train a meta-learner – typically a recurrent neural network – to predict the best hyperparameters for a given graph dataset. This allows the system to rapidly adapt to new graphs with minimal training, demonstrating a significant improvement in embedding quality compared to using fixed hyperparameters or single, pre-trained embeddings. We focus on the underlying mechanisms and theoretical implications of this approach, providing a framework for future research in adaptive graph representation learning.

title: 基于语义网的知识图谱推理与进化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning and evolution based on semantic networks. The core idea is to leverage the inference capabilities of semantic networks to perform reasoning and completion within a knowledge graph, coupled with evolutionary algorithms for dynamic adaptation and refinement. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning often relies on rule-based systems or limited statistical methods, which can struggle with complex relationships and evolving data. Our method addresses these limitations by utilizing semantic networks' inherent ability to represent and infer knowledge based on relationships between concepts. The evolutionary algorithm component allows the knowledge graph to adapt to new information and changes in relationships over time, ensuring its continued relevance and accuracy. We demonstrate the potential of this combined approach to significantly enhance the intelligence and maintainability of knowledge graphs. This work presents a framework for intelligent knowledge graph management, offering improvements in both reasoning accuracy and evolutionary robustness.

title: Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning for Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery, termed Quantum-Inspired Relational Reasoning (QIRR), which seeks to overcome the limitations of traditional statistical methods by incorporating principles from quantum mechanics. Classical causal discovery algorithms often struggle to discern genuine causal relationships from mere statistical correlations, frequently leading to spurious causal inferences. QIRR addresses this challenge by mimicking the superposition and interference phenomena observed in quantum systems. We propose a framework where multiple potential causal pathways are simultaneously explored, with probabilistic inference guided by simulated quantum measurements designed to identify pathways exhibiting stronger interference – a hallmark of causal strength. The core of QIRR lies in a probabilistic model incorporating conditional probabilities and interference terms, allowing the algorithm to evaluate the relative likelihood of different causal relationships. This approach offers the potential to identify more robust and accurate causal models compared to conventional statistical methods, particularly in scenarios with complex or noisy data. The paper outlines the key components of the QIRR framework, detailing the probabilistic model, the simulated quantum measurement process, and the inference procedure for determining the most likely causal relationships.

title: 自适应量子拓扑网络控制
abstract: Quantum topology networks (QTN) offer unprecedented control over quantum systems due to their inherent robustness and unique topological properties. This paper investigates a novel control algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum Topology Control," designed to harness these properties for automated network structure manipulation and state prediction. We propose a mechanism utilizing entangled qubits to dynamically adjust network topology, enabling precise and predictable behavior. The core claim centers on the ability of this algorithm to autonomously control a QTN, predicting its future state based on observed network evolution. This represents a significant advancement over traditional network control techniques, particularly when applied to complex, non-linear quantum systems. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, explores its potential applications, and provides a preliminary analysis of its performance.

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithm for Optimization
abstract: Quantum-inspired algorithms are emerging as a promising alternative to classical optimization techniques, particularly for complex problem domains. This paper introduces a novel quantum-inspired algorithm designed to leverage the principles of superposition and entanglement to enhance search and solution efficiency. We explore the potential of these concepts to represent and manipulate problem states, offering a fundamentally different approach to optimization. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around creating a quantum-like state space, enabling efficient exploration of the solution space. This work presents a preliminary analysis of the algorithm's potential for exponential speedups, although further investigation and validation are necessary.

title: Epistemic Bayesian Networks for Causal Discovery
abstract: Traditional causal discovery methods often assume complete knowledge of the system being studied, a simplifying assumption rarely met in real-world scenarios. This paper introduces Epistemic Bayesian Networks (EBNs), an extension of standard Bayesian Networks that explicitly incorporates the observer's knowledge and uncertainty. EBNs utilize 'epistemic nodes' to represent beliefs about the causal relationships between variables, informed by both prior knowledge and observational data. This approach addresses the limitations of conventional methods by accounting for the observer's subjective perspective, potentially leading to more accurate and robust causal inferences. The core mechanism involves defining and utilizing epistemic nodes within the network structure, with associated probability distributions reflecting the observer's confidence in different relationships. We explore the theoretical foundations of EBNs, outlining key concepts and proposing a framework for constructing and analyzing these networks. This work lays the groundwork for a new paradigm in causal discovery, where the observer's role is central to the process.

title: Hyperdimensional Temporal Logic
abstract: This paper introduces Hyperdimensional Temporal Logic (HTL), a novel approach to representing and reasoning about temporal relationships and causality. HTL leverages the principles of hyperdimensional computing – utilizing high-dimensional vectors (hypervectors) – to encode temporal information efficiently and perform complex computations. The core idea is to treat temporal sequences as hypervectors, enabling operations like temporal inference, causal reasoning, and temporal property verification through vector operations. Unlike traditional temporal logics that often struggle with scalability and expressiveness in complex scenarios, HTL aims to provide a more scalable and powerful framework. This work formally defines HTL, outlines its key components, and demonstrates its potential through a conceptual model. The paper highlights the advantages of this combined approach and sets the stage for future research in this area. ---

title: Fractal Algorithmic Geometry
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Fractal Algorithmic Geometry (FAG), a novel approach to algorithm design and optimization. The core premise is that higher-dimensional algorithmic spaces can be efficiently represented and navigated using fractal geometries. This allows for mapping algorithmic operations, such as sorting and searching, onto multi-fractal spaces where distances correlate with algorithmic efficiency. The system dynamically adapts its fractal structure based on operational load and data characteristics, creating a resilient and computationally efficient framework. This approach contrasts significantly with traditional Euclidean approaches, offering potential improvements in computational complexity and overall system performance. The paper details the theoretical foundations, the mapping process, and the dynamic adaptation mechanisms within FAG, arguing for its potential as a foundational element in future algorithm design.

title: On Behaviour Generation for Robots Based on Cognitive Architectures
abstract: This paper investigates the application of cognitive architectures to the generation of robust and adaptable behaviours in robotic systems. Traditional approaches to robot control often rely on hand-coded rules or complex, brittle algorithms, struggling to cope with the inherent uncertainties and complexities of real-world environments. We posit that a more effective approach lies in modelling the human cognitive process itself – a process characterized by situatedness, learning, and flexible reasoning – within a robotic system. This work proposes a framework leveraging cognitive architectures to achieve this, arguing that simulating human cognition offers a pathway to generating significantly more intelligent and adaptable robot behaviour. The core claim is the utilization of cognitive architectures to mimic human cognitive processes, leading to the creation of more intelligent and flexible robot behaviours. The central mechanism involves constructing a cognitive architecture incorporating modules for perception, memory, inference, and action, subsequently applied to robot control. This approach addresses limitations of traditional methods by providing a structured, biologically-inspired framework for robot behaviour. We explore the key components and considerations involved in designing such an architecture and discuss potential applications. ---

title: UniFusion: Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction via Unified Spatio-temporal Depth Alignment
abstract: In this paper, we address the challenging problem of 4D reconstruction from sparse-view videos. This setup usually relies on monocular depth estimation to provide priors for the reconstruction model. A key challenge arises from limited cross-view overlap and temporal variation, making monocular depth predictions inconsistent across views and time. Existing methods align spatial and temporal dimensions in separate stages, requiring foreground segmentation masks while failing to leverage temporal cues for cross-view alignment. Contrary to these methods, we propose a unified spatial-temporal depth alignment framework that jointly resolves cross-view and cross-time inconsistencies without distinguishing foreground/background. Our method represents depth maps across views and time as a set of spatio-temporal neural fields. This representation not only yields fast convergence, but also captures spatio-temporal correlation among depth maps implicitly, without dependence on external segmentation/tracking models. We also propose a multi-view depth-order loss while leveraging the classic scale-and-shift-invariant loss to further improve the final depth quality. The aligned depths initialize and supervise Gaussian splatting models for 4D reconstruction. Experiments on Ego-Exo4D and EgoHuman demonstrate that our improved depth alignment substantially benefits dynamic Gaussian-splatting-based reconstruction methods for novel-time/view synthesis and geometry accuracy/consistency.

title: Natural Language Processing for Real-Time Semantic Correlation of Shared Cyber Threat Indicators in National Defense
abstract: Defense intelligence systems receive continuous streams of natural-language threat reports in which the same event is frequently described using different terminology, structure, and coded language. Traditional keyword systems classify such reports as unrelated, fragmenting the intelligence picture and delaying coordinated response. This paper examines how Natural Language Processing (NLP) enables the real-time semantic correlation of shared cyber threat indicators. It reviews the progression from term-weighting and word embeddings to contextual transformer representations, and specifies an NLP pipeline that combines semantic encoding, similarity scoring, named-entity and relationship extraction, and clustering to link related threats into unified, analyst-ready groups. Using representative open-source and synthetic corpora, the study shows conceptually and through illustrative results that embedding-based correlation recognizes semantically equivalent reports that share few surface tokens, thereby exposing coordinated and evolving threats. The paper contributes a structured account of semantic correlation for defense CTI, a categorization of similarity thresholds into actionable intelligence bands, and a discussion of the operational and ethical conditions for deployment. The evaluation is illustrative rather than comparative: the behavior described and the similarity bands reported are indicative defaults presented together with a specified evaluation protocol and calibration procedure, not measured results, and the relationship of this work to the first author's earlier study of semantic correlation and de-duplication is disclosed and delineated explicitly. Subject to those qualifications, the findings suggest that NLP-driven correlation materially improves situational awareness and the speed of national defense response.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks in Large Language Models: A Systematic Literature Review on Taxonomy, Evaluation, and Mitigation (SLR Dataset)
abstract: This dataset contains the complete supporting material for the systematic literature review (SLR) "Prompt Injection Attacks in Large Language Models: A Systematic Literature Review on Taxonomy, Evaluation, and Mitigation." It documents every stage of the review, from the search and screening protocol through quality assessment to the final data extraction and synthesis, enabling the review to be independently audited and reproduced. The review followed the Kitchenham and Charters guidelines, with reporting aligned to PRISMA 2020. Literature was retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus, covering peer-reviewed articles published between January 2024 and March 2026. Of 271 initial records, 68 studies met all inclusion criteria and quality thresholds and form the primary corpus. The workbook comprises seven sheets: inclusion and exclusion criteria; abstract filtering criteria; the ten-item quality assessment checklist and rubrics; per-study quality scores and inclusion decisions; the full data-extraction table covering attacks, defenses, datasets, evaluation, and results across all 68 studies; a mapping of extracted data to the review's taxonomy and figures; and the research objectives with the exact Boolean search query. A README file describes each sheet in detail. Please cite the associated manuscript when using this dataset.

Literature was retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus, covering peer-reviewed articles published between January 2024 and March 2026. Of 271 initial records, 68 studies met all inclusion criteria and quality thresholds and form the primary corpus. The workbook comprises seven sheets: inclusion and exclusion criteria; abstract filtering criteria; the ten-item quality assessment checklist and rubrics; per-study quality scores and inclusion decisions; the full data-extraction table covering attacks, defenses, datasets, evaluation, and results across all 68 studies; a mapping of extracted data to the review's taxonomy and figures; and the research objectives with the exact Boolean search query. title: Based on Quantum Entanglement for Distributed Computing Resource Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for optimizing distributed computing resources. The core claim is that leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement can facilitate more efficient and low-latency communication and collaboration between distributed computing nodes, ultimately enhancing overall computational performance. The proposed system establishes "quantum links" between nodes through entanglement, bypassing traditional physical distance limitations and enabling instantaneous information transfer via entangled states. Advanced distributed algorithms, combined with the optimization of entanglement generation and maintenance, allow for dynamic task allocation, resource scheduling, and result consolidation. This research represents a novel approach to distributed computing resource optimization, addressing the limitations imposed by conventional communication bottlenecks, even within the current nascent stage of quantum computing. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future exploration into the practical implementation of entanglement-based distributed computing systems. ---

title: A Parallel Computing Architecture Based on Quantum State Superposition
abstract: This paper proposes a novel parallel computing architecture designed to leverage the principles of quantum state superposition for achieving superlinear computational speeds. The architecture centers around a network of parallel computing units capable of simultaneously processing multiple quantum states. Quantum entanglement plays a crucial role in facilitating information transfer and synchronization between quantum bits within this system. The core claim is that this design effectively utilizes superposition to unlock unprecedented computational capabilities. The architecture's innovative approach contributes to exploring the possibilities of quantum computing architecture and offers a new design paradigm for future quantum computation. This document details the architecture, key mechanisms, and theoretical considerations underpinning this approach.

title: Quantum-Inspired Clustering of High-Dimensional Data using Tensor Decomposition
abstract: High-dimensional data clustering remains a challenging problem in data science, largely due to the "curse of dimensionality" and the increased computational complexity associated with traditional clustering algorithms. This paper proposes a novel approach to high-dimensional data clustering by leveraging quantum-inspired tensor decomposition techniques. We introduce a framework that utilizes tensor networks to represent data as a hierarchy of interconnected components, allowing for efficient identification of clusters based on shared tensor structures. The core idea is inspired by quantum mechanics' representation of complex systems, specifically the ability to capture correlations and relationships within data through tensor networks. This method avoids the limitations of standard clustering algorithms that often struggle with the intricate dependencies inherent in high-dimensional data. The proposed technique demonstrates promising potential for improved clustering performance and scalability in scenarios involving complex, multi-faceted datasets. We present a detailed mathematical formulation and the key steps involved in the algorithm, along with a discussion of its theoretical underpinnings and potential applications.

title: 基于时间窗口的分布式机器学习
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed machine learning framework centered around the concept of time windows. Addressing the inherent challenges of data heterogeneity and communication latency prevalent in traditional distributed learning, our approach partitions data into independent time windows. Each window undergoes localized model training, fostering autonomy and reducing communication overhead. Subsequently, a model aggregation mechanism is employed to consolidate learning across windows, iteratively refining the global model. We demonstrate the potential of this strategy to significantly improve the efficiency and scalability of distributed machine learning systems. This work introduces a new paradigm for tackling distributed learning problems by leveraging temporal segmentation and intelligent model fusion. The core claim of this research is to design a framework capable of effectively handling data heterogeneity and communication delays, while the core mechanism relies on time window partitioning and model aggregation.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Graph Topological Features
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, including social network analysis, drug discovery, and recommendation systems. A crucial aspect of GNN performance is the selection and engineering of graph topological features. Traditionally, these features are painstakingly designed by domain experts, a process that is both time-consuming and often limited in scope. This paper proposes a novel self-supervised learning approach for automatically learning graph topological features. Our method leverages the inherent structural relationships within a graph to enable nodes to predict their own context, effectively creating rich and informative feature representations. We hypothesize that by allowing nodes to learn from their surroundings, we can generate more robust and generalizable topological features compared to manually engineered features. The core claim of this work is that manually engineered topological features often fail to generalize across different graph domains. The mechanism relies on a self-supervised task where nodes are trained to predict their immediate structural context. This automated feature engineering process promises to significantly improve the adaptability and performance of GNNs across diverse graph datasets.

title: Formal Modeling of Quantum Computing Hardware Reliability
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across various fields, yet its realization hinges critically on the reliability of its hardware. Unlike classical computing, quantum systems are exceptionally sensitive to environmental noise and prone to errors, leading to significant challenges in maintaining coherence and accurate computation. This research presents a formal model designed to rigorously analyze the reliability of quantum computing hardware. The model incorporates probabilistic representations of quantum gates and qubits, alongside noise models that capture various sources of error, and evaluates the effectiveness of fault-tolerance techniques. The core of the model is a simulation framework allowing for comprehensive evaluation of the impact of these factors on the overall system performance. This approach provides a quantitative basis for designing more robust quantum computing systems and optimizing operational strategies, moving beyond intuitive estimations and towards a scientifically grounded understanding of quantum hardware reliability. The model is presented with detailed formulas and mathematical notations, offering a precise and verifiable framework for analysis.

title: Meta-Learning for Program Transfer Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the application of meta-learning to program transfer learning, aiming to accelerate the learning process and improve the accuracy of new programs. Traditional program transfer learning often suffers from slow adaptation and suboptimal performance due to the need for extensive fine-tuning. Our core claim is that leveraging meta-learning, where a model learns *how* to learn programs, can significantly enhance the efficiency and precision of program transfer. We propose a framework where a meta-learning model is trained on a diverse set of programming tasks, enabling it to effectively guide the adaptation of a new program. The mechanism involves the meta-learner learning task-specific learning strategies, which are then applied to the target program during transfer. This approach demonstrates the potential to drastically reduce the learning time and improve the final performance compared to conventional methods. We present a theoretical analysis of the proposed approach and discuss its implications for various program domains.

title: Self-Organizing Metric Space for Wave Propagation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Self-Organizing Metric Space (SOM) architecture specifically designed to enhance wave propagation accuracy. The core challenge in wave propagation modeling lies in accurately capturing the complex interplay between wave direction, geometry, and propagation characteristics. Traditional methods often struggle to achieve this precision, particularly in scenarios involving intricate wave patterns. This work proposes a new SOM framework leveraging feedback loops to dynamically adjust the metric space, thereby optimizing wave propagation representations. This design mitigates the limitations of existing approaches by providing a more robust and adaptable solution for wave propagation modeling.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Transformations for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-adaptive topological transformations for enhancing the efficiency and stability of quantum computation. Traditional quantum algorithms often suffer from limitations in robustness and scalability, prompting the exploration of novel approaches. We propose a new method leveraging the unique properties of topological quantum states to dynamically adjust the geometry of the qubit system, mitigating errors and enhancing computational capabilities. This research focuses on the design of a self-adaptive transformation process that adapts to the specific noise characteristics of the quantum hardware, thereby improving overall performance. The core claim centers on the utilization of self-adaptive topological transformations to overcome inherent challenges in quantum computation. This work presents a novel framework demonstrating improved fidelity and extended coherence times in quantum simulations and computations. We aim to provide a foundation for future advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Cooperative Belief Formation
abstract: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but a significant challenge remains: effectively coordinating agents to achieve common goals. This paper addresses the limitations of current MARL approaches by introducing a novel framework centered around cooperative belief formation. The core claim is that existing MARL systems struggle to develop and maintain shared beliefs among agents, hindering their ability to work together effectively. Our approach introduces a dynamic mechanism allowing agents to continuously update their beliefs about the environment and the actions of other agents, based on observed data. This mechanism promotes a collaborative process of belief formation, leading to improved coordination and performance. The key innovation lies in explicitly modeling the process of belief updating as a learned component within the MARL system. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and present a detailed design, outlining the algorithm and key parameters. We analyze the impact of varying belief update frequencies and the level of trust between agents on the overall system performance. The results demonstrate that our framework significantly improves cooperative performance compared to traditional MARL methods, highlighting the importance of shared belief formation in complex multi-agent scenarios. The work contributes a valuable building block for more robust and scalable MARL systems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Neural Networks for Optimized Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum-inspired neural networks (QINNs) to optimize resource allocation problems. Traditional resource allocation algorithms often struggle with complex scenarios exhibiting non-convexities and high dimensionality. We propose a novel approach leveraging principles derived from quantum mechanics, specifically superposition and interference, to construct neural networks capable of efficiently navigating these challenges. The core idea is to design network architectures that emulate the patterns of quantum interference, effectively exploring multiple potential solutions simultaneously. We formulate the resource allocation problem as an optimization task and map it onto the QINN framework. The network's architecture is designed to promote constructive interference at optimal solutions while suppressing interference at suboptimal ones. The theoretical underpinnings of this approach are presented, along with a detailed explanation of the network structure and training methodology. Preliminary results demonstrate the potential of QINNs to outperform conventional optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios demanding a comprehensive search across the solution space. Further research will focus on scaling the approach to larger, more complex resource allocation problems and exploring the interplay between quantum-inspired mechanisms and classical optimization methods.

title: Bio-Inspired Adaptive Neural Networks for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm leveraging the principles of bio-inspired adaptive neural networks. The core claim is to design an algorithm capable of automatically adjusting network structure and learning strategies, ultimately enhancing learning efficiency and stability. The proposed method mimics biological neural systems by dynamically modifying network connection weights and neuron numbers based on environmental feedback. Traditional RL algorithms often rely on pre-defined network architectures and learning rules, limiting their adaptability. This work addresses this limitation by introducing a biologically-inspired approach that allows the network to self-organize and optimize its learning process. The algorithm incorporates a feedback mechanism that allows it to respond to changes in the environment, improving its ability to tackle complex and dynamic challenges. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of both the network architecture and the learning strategy, offering a potentially more robust and efficient solution for RL problems. The algorithm is evaluated theoretically and conceptually, outlining its design principles and anticipated benefits.

title: Autogenous Room-Temperature Topological Phononic Qutrit Architecture Utilizing Bogoliubov Pressure and AI-Directed Assembly
abstract: This repository contains the mathematical blueprint, technical specifications, and commercial unit economics for a 300K non-equilibrium quantum processor. By utilizing a localized Bogoliubov phonon pressure trap and a Universal Dielectric Barrier Discharge (U-DBD) plasma acoustic mirror (R -> 1), this architecture fundamentally bypasses the cryogenic thermodynamic limits of the current superconducting paradigm. Core Deliverables: Theoretical Preprint: Mathematical proof of the 300K Bogoliubov pressure trap and ternary state encoding (|-1>, |0>, |1>). USPTO Provisional Specification: Engineering mechanics for the U-DBD micro-vascular plasma waveguide and AI-STM atomic assembly protocols. Commercial & Logistics Addendum: Unit economic breakdown detailing the CapEx/OpEx reduction from the USD 3M+ cryogenic baseline down to the USD 45K to 85K solid-state form factor. Systems Architecture Schematic: Visual stack mapping the integration of the PSAS neuromorphic controller, UL-SMF interposer, and LAB-Q thermo-acoustic backplane. Commercial Availability: This architecture is released under CC BY 4.0 to eliminate evaluation friction. Lawrence Architectures is actively seeking tier-one simulation, High-Performance Computing (HPC), and fabrication partnerships to run multiphysics benchmarks. The framework is currently open for Option to Evaluate (OTE) agreements: inquiries@lawrencearchitectures.com
